query: High-entropy alloys can combine mechanical strength, wear resistance, corrosion protection, oxidation resistance, and thermal stability, while their large compositional space offers opportunities to tune degradation in harsh environments. Prior studies have largely considered wear and corrosion separately, and only a few reports address their combined action, leaving the governing behavior poorly understood. For a high-entropy alloy subjected to tribo-corrosion, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs the coupled response and why? Describe a controlled comparison that would isolate the governing cause, predict changes in total degradation and its wear and corrosion components relative to a matched baseline, state where the prediction should hold or fail, connect it to the available prior evidence, and identify a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In tribo-corrosion of high-entropy alloys, the cyclic formation and mechanical disruption of a protective oxide film is the key mechanism that couples wear and corrosion. When the oxide film is intact, it passivates the alloy from corrosion; however, wear processes continuously remove the film, exposing reactive surfaces that rapidly corrode, which in turn alter the wear behavior.
generation.material_initial_state: A high-entropy alloy with a naturally formed, uniform passivating oxide layer under ambient conditions.
generation.intervention: Expose alloy samples to controlled tribo-corrosion tests where the integrity of the oxide layer is either preserved (by minimizing wear or enhancing oxide stability) or deliberately disrupted (by increasing wear intensity or pre-abrading the surface).
generation.conditions: Tests are performed under identical mechanical load, temperature, and electrolyte pH with two conditions: (a) a corrosive electrolyte and mechanical wear combined (tribo-corrosion), and (b) baseline tests with either only mechanical wear in an inert medium or only static corrosion without wear.
generation.structural_mediator: The protective oxide film on the alloy surface and its mechanical stability.
generation.mechanism: Under tribo-corrosion conditions, mechanical wear intermittently removes the stable oxide film, exposing fresh, reactive metal surfaces. These exposed surfaces undergo accelerated corrosion. The corrosion products may further modify wear characteristics. The net degradation rate is thus governed by the dynamic balance between oxide film reformation (which suppresses corrosion) and its mechanical disruption (which promotes it).
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline, the coupled condition will exhibit increased total degradation with higher rates of both wear loss and corrosion depth. Samples in which the oxide film is better maintained will show lower degradation, while those with deliberate oxide disruption will show significantly higher degradation. The synergistic effect of wear and corrosion should be evident as a greater combined material loss than the simple sum of the individual processes.
generation.baseline: Tribological wear tests performed in inert media (to isolate the wear component) and static corrosion tests (to isolate the corrosion component) will each show lower degradation rates compared to the coupled tribo-corrosion scenario.
generation.boundary: This prediction should hold when the protective oxide film is the primary barrier against corrosion. It may fail if other microstructural features (such as grain-boundary strengthening or elemental segregation) dominate the material’s response, or if the testing environment significantly limits oxide regrowth (e.g., very high oxidizing conditions where even disrupted films reform too rapidly or inert conditions where corrosion is inherently suppressed).
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of the synergistic increase in degradation is uncertain and may vary with subtle changes in alloy composition, oxide film characteristics, and test conditions. Quantitative separation of wear and corrosion contributions under dynamic oxide film behavior also remains to be fully established.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct paired tribo-corrosion tests on identical high-entropy alloy samples. One set will be pre-treated to form a thicker, more stable oxide film (using anodic pre-oxidation or a controlled atmosphere) and another set will be mechanically pre-abraded to remove the oxide film. All tests should be performed under identical mechanical load, temperature, and corrosive electrolyte conditions. In-situ surface characterization (e.g., XPS or Raman spectroscopy) should be used to monitor oxide film integrity during testing.
measurements: Wear track depth and profile analysis
Real-time measurements of oxide film thickness
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If samples with an intact, pre-established oxide film show no significant reduction in overall degradation or in the individual wear and corrosion components compared to the pre-abraded samples, then the hypothesis that oxide film dynamics mediate the synergistic coupling between wear and corrosion is falsified.
